what: Zimmer Biomet makes orthopaedic implants: artificial knees, hips, shoulders and spine and trauma hardware, plus the robotic systems and instruments used to place them.
money: shoulder, foot and ankle, and trauma products
moat: Surgeons trained on its instruments and implant systems, with hospital contracts and inventory consigned on site, which makes switching a retraining exercise.
risks: Return on invested capital of about 5% is low for a medical device company
Hospital pricing pressure on implants is persistent
Debt of about $7.5 billion against little cash
Weight-loss medicines could reduce obesity-related joint replacement over time
opportunities: Revenue grew about 7% last year with a 70% gross margin
An ageing population raises the number of joint replacements every year
Its robotic surgery system and newer implants have been gaining share
watch: Knee and hip revenue growth and robotic system placements.
